chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Bishr ibn Maslama, and others, from the one who informed them, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The best loan is that which attracts benefit.
ai.seo_question: What is the best type of loan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that the superior quality of an interest-free loan (qard) lies in its capacity to generate mutual benefit, a principle that underpins the Shia jurisprudence of avoiding riba (usury). This narration highlights the ethical dimension of lending, where the 'benefit' may manifest as gratitude, a gift, or ease for the borrower, thereby distinguishing it from commercial transactions that prioritize profit over social welfare. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how qard functions not merely as a financial instrument but as a means of fostering social cohesion and divine pleasure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Bishr Bin Maslama, and someone else, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The best loan is what attracts the benefits’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Bishr ibn Muslimah from more than one person who reported who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The best loan is that which attracts benefits.’”
